fields.body_md:
## About this programme

Newcastle University Business School runs a full-time MBA (programme code 5823F) on its Newcastle city centre campus. The course lasts 12 months, is taught on campus in English, and starts in September 2027.

The programme has three phases of modules, covering subjects such as finance, marketing, strategy, operations and entrepreneurship. You also choose two electives, and complete a consultancy project with a live client. The module list on the course page is an example, published before each year.

The most important thing for an Indian applicant: you need a 2:1 degree (or an equivalent) and at least three years of full-time work after your degree, with managerial responsibility.

## Can you get in?

**Your degree.** You need a 2:1 honours degree, or an international equivalent. A 2:1 is a UK degree grade. For an Indian degree, the grade that counts depends on the university you studied at. Newcastle sorts Indian universities into three sections. At a Section 1 university, a 2:1 means 60% or a CGPA of 6.0 out of 10. CGPA stands for cumulative grade point average.

**Work experience.** You need the equivalent of at least three years of significant, full-time work after your degree, with managerial responsibility. Exceptional applicants without the degree may be considered with more than five years of experience.

**GMAT.** The GMAT is a business school admissions test. You do not need to take it to study this MBA.

**English.** You need IELTS (International English Language Testing System) 6.5 overall, with at least 6.0 in each sub-skill. This is higher than the university's general rule of 5.5 in each sub-skill.

**Selection.** You send academic transcripts, a CV, a personal statement, English test results if you need to show them, and two referees. A referee is a person who writes a reference for you. All selected applicants are interviewed. You are also considered for MBA scholarships at interview.

## What it costs

**Tuition** for the full 12-month programme is **£34,400**.

**Deposit.** Students from India must pay a **£3,000** tuition deposit, or send an official sponsorship letter, by **27 August 2027**. A deposit is an advance payment that secures your place. A sponsorship letter is an official letter from the person or organisation paying for your studies. The deposit is non-refundable, and it is taken off your tuition when you register. If you need an ATAS certificate (explained under visa documents below), the date is **13 August 2027**.

**Money for your visa.** The UK student visa asks you to show that you can pay your living costs. This is money you show, not a fee to the university. Newcastle is outside London, so the rate for courses outside London applies: **£1,171** for each month of your course, for up to **9 months**. You must have had this money for **28 days in a row**. The last day of that 28-day period must be within **31 days** of the day you apply.

### First-year example

| Item | How it is worked out | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| Tuition | Full programme | £34,400 |
| Visa living money | £1,171 × 9 months | £10,539 |
| Student visa application fee | Applying from outside the UK | £558 |
| Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS) | £776 for each year of your visa | £776 or more |
| **First-year total** | £34,400 + £10,539 + £558 + £776 | **at least £46,273** |

Your visa lasts longer than your course, so you usually pay for more than one year. A 16-month visa costs £1,164: £776 plus half of £776 (£388).

This is an example, not a budget. It leaves out flights, rent and everyday spending. Amounts change, so confirm them on gov.uk before you apply.

Newcastle says new international students are guaranteed accommodation for one year, subject to certain conditions.

Read the [UK student visa guide](/study-abroad/visas/uk-student-visa-guide) for the full rules. To compare costs across UK universities, use the [UK total cost breakdown](/study-abroad/study-in/uk/uk-total-cost-breakdown).

### Other visa documents

- **A CAS** (Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies). Your course provider issues it, and you need it to apply.
- **A valid passport.**
- **English at CEFR level B2 or above.** CEFR is a common scale for rating language ability. Your university can assess your English itself.
- **A TB test, if you need one.** India is on the UK list of countries where the test applies. You need the test if all three of these are true: you are coming to the UK for 6 months or more; you have lived in a listed country for 6 months or more; you were living in a listed country within the last 6 months. The test must be done at a clinic approved by the Home Office.
- **An ATAS certificate, if your course needs one.** ATAS is the Academic Technology Approval Scheme. Indian nationals are not on the exempt list. You must have the certificate before you start the course.

## Funding

Newcastle lists these awards for international students. Check each award page for the courses it covers.

- **Vice-Chancellor's Excellence award.** Up to 50% of tuition, for students assessed as international for fee purposes. You must have applied for your degree offer by 31 May 2027. The scholarship deadline is 8 June 2027. Apply through the Apply to Newcastle Portal.
- **MBA scholarships.** You are considered for MBA scholarships at interview.
- **General line.** The MBA course page says you may be eligible for a scholarship worth 25% off the international fee.

For all of Newcastle's funding, see the [global scholarships page](https://www.ncl.ac.uk/study/global-scholarships/).

## Deadlines and intakes

There is no application closing date. The course starts in September 2027. Newcastle suggests international students apply at least two months before the start.

You cannot apply for your visa earlier than 6 months before the course starts, so plan your visa application after your offer.

| Date | What is due |
|---|---|
| 31 May 2027 | Degree offer applied for (Vice-Chancellor's Excellence award) |
| 8 June 2027 | Vice-Chancellor's Excellence scholarship deadline |
| 13 August 2027 | Deposit or sponsorship letter, if your course needs an ATAS certificate |
| 27 August 2027 | £3,000 deposit or sponsorship letter, for students from India |

## How to apply

1. Check that you meet the entry rules: a 2:1 or equivalent, three years of managerial work experience, and IELTS 6.5 with 6.0 in each sub-skill.
2. Apply online through the Apply to Newcastle Portal. Scholarship applications use the same portal.
3. Send your academic transcripts, CV, personal statement, English test results if needed, and the details of two referees.
4. Attend an interview. All selected applicants are interviewed.
5. Pay the £3,000 deposit, or send an official sponsorship letter, by 27 August 2027.
6. Get your CAS from Newcastle. Then apply for your visa, following the [UK student visa guide](/study-abroad/visas/uk-student-visa-guide).

## After the programme

- **Graduate visa.** This lets you stay and work in the UK after your course. It lasts 2 years if you apply on or before 31 December 2026, and 18 months if you apply on or after 1 January 2027. The application fee is £937.
- **Careers support.** A Careers Consultant offers one-to-one coaching.
- **Outcomes.** Newcastle's course page says 91% of graduates are in work or further study 15 months after graduation. The figure comes from the Graduate Outcomes Survey, 2018/19 to 2023/24.
- **Accreditation.** Newcastle University Business School is accredited by AACSB, EQUIS and AMBA. The page says AMBA has accredited it for over 35 years.

## Who it suits

**A strong choice if:**

- You have at least three years of full-time work with managerial responsibility.
- You want a consultancy project with a live client.
- You want a business school accredited by AACSB, EQUIS and AMBA.
- You want the option of the Graduate visa after your course.

**Think carefully if:**

- You have less than three years of work experience, or no managerial responsibility in it.
- You cannot reach IELTS 6.5 with 6.0 in each sub-skill.
- You cannot pay the deposit or show the visa money set out in the cost section.

faq_json.q: Does the Newcastle MBA need the GMAT?
faq_json.a: No. Newcastle says you do not need to take the GMAT to study its MBA.

faq_json.q: What IELTS score does the Newcastle MBA need?
faq_json.a: IELTS 6.5 overall, with at least 6.0 in each sub-skill. This is higher than the university's general rule of 5.5 in each sub-skill.

faq_json.q: How much work experience do I need for the Newcastle MBA?
faq_json.a: At least three years of significant, full-time work after your degree, with managerial responsibility. Exceptional applicants without the degree may be considered with more than five years of experience.

faq_json.q: What is the application deadline for the Newcastle MBA?
faq_json.a: There is no closing date. The course starts in September 2027, and Newcastle suggests applying at least two months before the start.

faq_json.q: How much is the tuition deposit for students from India?
faq_json.a: £3,000, or an official sponsorship letter, by 27 August 2027. The deposit is non-refundable and is taken off your tuition when you register.
